notes.note: هٰذَا لَيْسَ رُخَامًا، بَلْ مَرْمَر: in dictionaries both رُخَام and مَرْمَر are 'marble'; 'alabaster' as مَرْمَر is Egyptian usage (مسجد المرمر). Correct for the story, but a learner may later find مرمر glossed as marble; consider adding '(in Egypt: alabaster)' to the gloss.
دَلِيلَتُكُمُ (a woman guide) is attested but دَلِيل is commonly used for both genders; fine as is.

Day 82 writes the greeting as تَحِيَّة طَيِّبَة وَبَعْدُ (pausal) and day 84 as تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ (accusative). Both are accepted; the accusative is the form found in real letters, so the two days could be made consistent.
الْكَهْرَبَاءُ هُنَا تُصْنَعُ مِنَ الشَّمْس is understandable but unidiomatic; natural MSA is تُوَلَّدُ (is generated) or تُنْتَجُ.
أَنَا صَنَعْتُ الشَّرَائِحَ (I made the slides) is fine; أَعْدَدْتُ would be the more usual verb.
The intro says لٰكِنَّهُ = 'but it' and مَعَ أَنَّهُ = 'although it', but the shared tap glosses say 'but he' / 'that he'. Not wrong, but 'but he/it' and 'that he/it' would match the lesson.
Tap gloss أَهَمُّ=the most important in a comparative sentence (أَهَمُّ مِنَ = more important than); the segs are right. Consider 'more important; the most important'.
Story logic: 'It's the second-to-last week of the course' but day 88 is in week 13, which day 85 calls the last week.
مَقَالَة is tapped as 'article (in a newspaper or magazine)' while the lesson uses it for Daniel's essay; the segs say 'an essay'. Consider 'article; essay'.
الَّذِي = 'the one who' and الَّتِي = 'who (f)' are fine for people but the lesson uses them for things ('the word which'); 'who, which, that' would cover both.

summary: I read the whole export for days 81–90 (3,123 lines): every Arabic line with its harakat, case endings and agreement, every seg and tap gloss, every mistakes pair, every quiz key and the transliterations. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: I found no misspelt word, no wrong case ending, no wrong verb form and no wrong quiz answer across the ten days; the passive, إِذَا + past, أَنَّ/لٰكِنَّ + accusative, duals, non-human plural agreement and the formal-letter formulas are all correct. The 24 findings are 5 major and 19 minor. The real problems are in the shared tap glosses, which are reused from earlier lessons and sometimes carry the wrong sense or the wrong form into the new context: اِكْتَشَفَ glossed as 'was discovered' (defeating the active/passive contrast), قِيلَ glossed 'it is said' on a quiz distractor, عَبَّرَ glossed as an imperative, عُنْوَان glossed 'address' in the headline lesson, plus several minor sense mismatches (عَشَرَ 'part of fifteen', السَّاعَةَ 'at the hour', عَفْوًا 'you're welcome', و 'and' in a letter list). One mistakes pair (day 90, شَرِيكُ الْمُحَادَثَةِ) marks a correct, common phrase as wrong. The transliteration engine has one systematic fault worth fixing: الِاحْتِرَام / الِاسْتِمَاع / الِامْتِحَان come out as 'liāḥtirām / liāstimāʿ / Iliāmtiḥān', which affects the title of day 89 and the closing formula of day 82; smaller engine quirks (Wabiālʾiḍāfati, maqhanā, Illatī, shāī/wāū, ashalu, raʾī, 'A / at', 'Wasāmī') are reported once each with examples. Ten notes cover register, consistency and story logic.
